subject: Annex: Capacity uplift & pricing corridor — review and legal redlines
messages:
From: Ruth Adams <ruth.adams@acmehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Annex A — Request to uplift committed throughput and pricing corridor

Jonas / team,

Thanks for the quick call this morning. As discussed, Acme needs a formal annex to the MSA to uplift committed capacity for Q4 beta and to add a pricing corridor for burst usage. Attached is a draft Annex A (redline requested). High-level asks: 

- Add 400 additional GPU-hours/week (phased over two months)
- Define a pricing corridor for bursts between 100–150% of commit (cap + discount matrix)
- Short clause for rollback rights if performance/regression happens during pilot

Can you review and confirm whether the proposed fee table and the rollback language are acceptable? We'd like to get commercial signoff by end of next week if possible.

Attachments: Annex A - Capacity Uplift v1.docx

Thanks,
Ruth
Ruth Adams
Director, Cloud Procurement
Acme Health
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ruth Adams <ruth.adams@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Annex A — Request to uplift committed throughput and pricing corridor

Ruth — thanks, received and reviewed quickly. High level: we can accommodate the uplift but need to align on three items before legal will greenlight the annex: 

1) Implementation timeline — agree phase dates and cutover testing window (we propose 2-week validation with KPIs)
2) Pricing corridor mechanics — need clarity on what triggers the higher corridor and how token accounting is reconciled; suggest the attached sample fee matrix change and a cap at 160% as upper bound
3) Rollback & SLA interactions — we prefer a mitigation window and credits instead of unilateral rollback; legal to propose language.

I've attached our internal redlines (Redlines_AnnexA_v2.pdf) and looped in Karthik and Laura to coordinate legal/commercial edits. Next steps: Karthik/legal to send a short redline by EOD Wed; if Acme agrees, we'll prepare a DocuSign packet for signatures.

Jonas Weber
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redlines_AnnexA_v2.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 20 Aug 2025 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Annex A redline notes (commercial + legal)

Team — quick internal notes before I share back to Acme. I kept this tight to avoid too many iteration rounds. Main changes in the attached PDF. Key points for discussion: 

- Fee matrix: we accepted the phased uplift but adjusted the burst corridor to 120–160% with a tiered per-token uplift (0–120% = standard; 120–140% = +12%; 140–160% = +20%). We added a monthly reconciliation clause to true-up usage.
- Rollback: removed 'unilateral rollback' language. Proposed: two-week mitigation/testing window, explicit regression KPIs, and an emergency rollback pathway that requires a joint ops call + 48-hour notice to exercise.
- SLA & credits: defined that credits for performance/regressions apply only to latency/availability regressions tied to Redwood runtime changes; not to model-quality metrics.
- Termination risk: added a short safety valve limiting termination for temporary capacity issues during pilot, but preserved normal termination rights thereafter.

Markus — please confirm whether the emergency rollback pathway and 48-hour notice works from infra/ops perspective. Laura — can you review the credit carve-out language and make sure procurement will accept the limitation to runtime regressions only?

I'll produce a clean redline to send to Ruth once we confirm.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Ruth Adams <ruth.adams@acmehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>, Gideon Park <gideon.park@lawfirmllp.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Annex A — Request to uplift committed throughput and pricing corridor

Jonas / Karthik,

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear redlines. A couple of quick notes from Acme legal/procurement after a first pass with Gideon: 

- The tiered uplift percentages look reasonable; procurement requests the upper cap remain at 170% (they want a slightly wider burst window for holiday testing). Could Redwood meet 170% ceiling if we add an additional monthly reconciliation reporting requirement?
- The 48-hour notice for emergency rollback is acceptable only if Acme has the right to pause traffic immediately for data-safety incidents; suggest an explicit carve-out for data-safety emergencies.
- Gideon will provide minor language tweaks to the mitigation KPIs and will upload a tracked version by EOD tomorrow.

We remain on track for approvals next week if we can land on the cap and the data-safety carve-out. Happy to hop on a quick 20-min call today at 4 pm PT to resolve the cap question.

Ruth
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ruth Adams <ruth.adams@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Annex A — Request to uplift committed throughput and pricing corridor

Ruth — thanks, and good call earlier today. Quick summary and agreed actions (so procurement has a single source of truth):

- Cap: Redwood accepts a 170% burst ceiling for the pilot only, conditional on a monthly reconciliation report and a defined upper bound spend alert (ops alert at 150% usage).
- Data-safety carve-out: agreed — Acme may pause traffic immediately on verified data-safety incidents; that right is separate from rollback for performance regressions. We'll add a short definition of 'data-safety incident' and a 24-hour post-pause sync protocol.
- Doc flow: Gideon to upload tracked edits by EOD Fri; Karthik to review and provide final redline Saturday morning. If redlines match commercial notes, we'll produce a DocuSign packet by Monday and aim to have signatures by mid-next-week.

Attachments moved to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Acme-AnnexA-Working
DocuSign (pending): https://docusign.com/tx/XYZ-AnnexA

I'll follow up with the DocuSign packet once legal signs off. Thanks all — moving to execution.

Jonas Weber
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0187
